Hi Wojciech,


I think this is all a function of these choice RT models requiring many observations to get accurate parameter estimates. Before continuing, I think it would be best to simulate more than 500 trials (e.g. 2000 or more is probably best) and checking if you can recover parameters from those data. I think that with only 500 trials for a single subject, the data are not offering strong enough evidence to shift the priors by much. In this case, the posteriors are so wide that the mean does not give much information.


That said, recovery tends to work much better with fewer trials when there are multiple subjects. I have attached an image here showing the results of a parameter recovery that I ran on the LBA with 5 subjects worth of data (500 trials per condition). You can see that the extreme estimates get pulled toward the group averages, but overall the models recover the ranking of the parameters well. 


Anyway, I hope this helps. Let me know if you still get strange results with more simulated data. 


Best,

Nate
